Fuelwood provision values the woody biomass that households and local economies burn for
cooking and heating. The account carries the CAS team's per-country results; their staged
appendix documents the chain, and rebuilding it from the public inputs is the recorded
later step.

## Quantity

National annual fuelwood harvest volumes from FAO forestry statistics, converted to energy
content in terajoules, following the CAS methodology appendix.

## Price

The replacement cost of the equivalent energy from substitute fuels, per terajoule, in
constant 2019 USD, following the same appendix.

## Valuation

$$
\text{GEP}_i = \text{gross replacement value}_i - \text{human inputs}_i
$$

the ecosystem-attributable fraction of each country's gross fuelwood value, as the CAS
appendix defines it. The library reads their per-country results sheet, whose own title
states the values in thousands of 2019 USD, onto the account's country list.

## Coverage

The published table is one row for each of the account's 250 countries, base year 2019, in
constant 2019 USD. The CAS sheet values 180 countries; 179 join the account list by ISO3
and one, the Netherlands Antilles (dissolved 2010), cannot be carried and is written beside
the table with its value rather than dropped. The remaining rows are missing, not zero: the
sheet reports no value for them. A zero would mean a computed zero, and the sheet carries
none.

## Inputs

All paths come from `es_parameters.csv` under the `fuelwood_provision` service key: the CAS
per-country results sheet, with its source row beside it. The CAS appendix documents
(methodology, input data, code, output result) are staged beside the account's copy of the
results in base_data.
